stories.headline: AppsFlyer raises over $1B from Google, Meta, Unity and Moloco at $2.7B valuation

key_facts.fact: Ad-measurement firm AppsFlyer raised more than $1 billion in Series E funding at a $2.7 billion post-money valuation, with Moloco, Google, Meta and Unity each acquiring a minority stake.
key_facts.excerpt: AppsFlyer has raised more than $1 billion in Series E funding at a $2.7 billion post-money valuation... Moloco, Google, Meta and Unity have each acquired a minority stake in AppsFlyer.

key_facts.fact: CEO and co-founder Oren Kaniel said the investments are minority, non-controlling, non-exclusive, and that each investor is integrated with AppsFlyer but will not receive preferential treatment; the transaction is subject to regulatory approvals.

key_facts.fact: AppsFlyer said it will use the capital to accelerate AI-powered advertising measurement, cross-platform attribution and infrastructure to support autonomous marketing and AI-driven workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: AppsFlyer said it intends to use the capital to accelerate innovation in AI-powered advertising measurement, advance cross-platform attribution and measurement capabilities, and continue building infrastructure designed to support autonomous marketing and AI-driven workflows.

key_facts.fact: The San Francisco-based company works with more than 15,000 brands, has about 1,300 employees, and had previously raised $300 million, including a 2020 General Atlantic-led Series D of $210 million at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: The SF-based company works with more than 15,000 brands globally and has about 1,300 employees. The company has previously raised $300 million. Its General Atlantic-led 2020 Series D was $210 million at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation.

stories.headline: Chevron and Microsoft sign 20-year deal for 2.67 GW gas-powered West Texas data center (Project Kilby)

key_facts.fact: Chevron announced a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to develop a co-located natural-gas power facility (Project Kilby) supplying dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center in West Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: Chevron Corporation today announced that Energy Forge One LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary, has signed an agreement with Microsoft Corp. to develop a co-located power facility in West Texas that will provide dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center under a 20-year power purchase agreement.

key_facts.fact: Project Kilby is expected to deliver approximately 2.67 gigawatts of capacity, consuming roughly the power needed for about two million homes, making it among the largest co-located natural gas power and data center developments in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: The data center, called Project Kilby, is expected to consume nearly 2.7 gigawatts of electricity, equivalent to the power needed to run about two million homes.

key_facts.fact: A majority of the generation will come from large GE Vernova turbines, with additional capacity from Solar Turbines, a Caterpillar subsidiary; the plant will have its own on-site power fueled by Chevron's Permian Basin natural gas in Reeves County.
key_facts.excerpt: Two large GE Vernova turbines will generate most of the power, with a Caterpillar subsidiary Solar Turbines providing the rest... Microsoft will buy power from the power plant for 20 years.

key_facts.fact: Chevron expects a final investment decision by the end of 2026 after acquiring necessary permits, with first power delivery anticipated in 2028; Microsoft said the multi-billion-dollar investment over five to seven years would support over 6,000 construction jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: The multi-billion-dollar data center investment, spanning the next five to seven years, is expected to support over 6,000 construction jobs... Project Kilby is expected to provide first power by 2028 and will ramp up to 2.67 gigawatts over time.

stories.headline: China's all-CPU LineShine dethrones El Capitan as world's fastest supercomputer at 2.198 exaflops

key_facts.fact: China's LineShine debuted atop the 67th TOP500 ranking, the first time a China-based system has led since Sunway TaihuLight in 2017, ending El Capitan's run at No. 1.
key_facts.excerpt: The debut of China's LineShine on the 67th edition of the TOP500 rankings ends El Capitan's run at the top the list and marks the first time a China-based system has led the rankings since Sunway TaihuLight in 2017.

key_facts.fact: Installed at the National Supercomputing Centre in Shenzhen, LineShine achieved 2.198 exaflops on the High Performance Linpack benchmark, more than 20% ahead of No. 2 El Capitan, and is the world's fifth exascale system.
key_facts.excerpt: LineShine achieved 2.198 exaflops on the High Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark, putting it more than 20% ahead of the No. 2-ranked El Capitan system at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

key_facts.fact: LineShine reached the top spot with a domestic CPU-only design built around China's LingKun platform, proprietary LingQi interconnect and Kylin OS, using nearly 14 million cores (LX2 304-core 1.55GHz processors, 13,789,440 total cores).
key_facts.excerpt: LineShine reached the top spot with a domestic CPU-only design built around China's LingKun platform, proprietary LingQi interconnect, and Kylin operating system.

key_facts.fact: It is the first supercomputer to officially exceed 2 exaflops on the Linpack benchmark; the announcement was made at the ISC26 conference in Hamburg, Germany.
key_facts.excerpt: The custom-built cluster composed of nearly 14 million ARM cores is the first to officially exceed 2 exaflops on TOP500's Linpack benchmark... unveiled today at ISC26 in Hamburg, Germany.

key_facts.fact: Experts said the result reflects Beijing's drive for self-sufficiency more than its AI standing: LineShine ranked only fourth on a benchmark designed to simulate AI-like work, and China had stopped submitting systems for three years amid US chip export controls.
key_facts.excerpt: the results may say more about Beijing's desire to show self-sufficiency in computing systems than its standing in the global AI race, experts said... LineShine ranked fourth on a benchmark test designed to simulate computing work that is more similar to AI.

stories.headline: Definium's LSD-based DT120 hits primary endpoint in Phase 3 depression trial

key_facts.fact: Definium Therapeutics announced Monday June 22 positive topline results from Emerge, its first Phase 3 trial of DT120 (lysergide, an LSD formulation), a single 100 µg dose in adults with major depressive disorder; the trial met its primary endpoint with a statistically significant improvement versus placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: Emerge met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement from baseline compared with placebo, as measured by the change in MADRS total score at week 6.

key_facts.fact: At week 6, the DT120 group showed an LS mean change in MADRS total score of -13.3 versus -5.2 for placebo, an LS mean difference of -8.1 points (p<0.0001); the effect appeared rapid (week 1) and durable (week 12).
key_facts.excerpt: The LS mean change from baseline in MADRS total score at Week 6 in participants who received DT120 ODT 100 µg was -13.3 compared with -5.2 for patients who received placebo, a LS mean difference of -8.1 points (p<0.0001).

key_facts.fact: The trial involved 149 participants; about 35% of DT120 users substantially responded by week 6 (≥50% reduction) versus 7% of placebo, and 12% reached remission versus 3% of placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: About 35% of DT120 users had also substantially responded by week 6... compared to 7% of placebo users, while 12% experienced a remission (compared to 3% of the placebo group).

key_facts.fact: Definium is awaiting topline results from a second Phase 3 trial (Ascend) and plans to seek breakthrough therapy designation and expedited approval from the FDA; regulators typically require two positive trials.
key_facts.excerpt: Definium is still awaiting the primary results of its second double-blinded, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of DT120 for depression, codenamed Ascend... the company is planning to seek breakthrough therapy designation from the FDA for DT120.

sources.title: Definium Therapeutics Announces Positive Topline Results from Phase 3 Emerge Study of DT120 in Major Depressive Disorder

stories.headline: FDA reverses course on Regenxbio's Hunter syndrome gene therapy, opens accelerated-approval path

key_facts.fact: Regenxbio announced Monday June 22 that the FDA agreed existing clinical data are sufficient to support an accelerated-approval filing for Navsunli (clemidsogene lanparvovec, RGX-121), a one-time gene therapy for Mucopolysaccharidosis II (Hunter syndrome) — a reversal about four months after a February 2026 rejection.
key_facts.excerpt: the FDA has agreed that existing clinical data are sufficient to support an accelerated approval filing for Navsunli (clemidsogene lanparvovec), a one-time gene therapy for Mucopolysaccharidosis II (MPS II), also known as Hunter syndrome.

key_facts.fact: The FDA confirmed no additional studies are required and that it would not need an untreated control arm it had previously recommended; the company will request a Type A meeting in July and resubmit the BLA in Q3 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: FDA confirmed no additional studies required, existing longer-term data from the CAMPSIITE study will be reviewed on an expedited basis for approval via the accelerated approval pathway... The Company expects to resubmit the BLA in Q3 2026.

key_facts.fact: The move is part of a broader easing toward rare-disease candidates under new FDA leadership; the prior week the agency made a similar U-turn on uniQure's Huntington's disease gene therapy AMT-130.
key_facts.excerpt: In another sign that the FDA is easing its stance toward rare disease drug candidates under new leadership, the agency will reconsider Regenxbio's gene therapy for an ultra-rare childhood disease... last week, uniQure announced that the FDA made a U-turn, agreeing that phase 1/2 data for the Huntington's disease therapy, AMT-130, would suffice.

key_facts.fact: Approval of Navsunli could result in a Priority Review Voucher, which Regenxbio retains 100% of the proceeds from; the therapy would be commercialized by Nippon Shinyaku.
key_facts.excerpt: Approval of NAVSUNLI could result in receipt of a Priority Review Voucher (PRV). REGENXBIO retains all rights to, and 100 percent of any proceeds related to the potential sale of, the PRV.

stories.headline: Five Eyes cyber agencies warn frontier AI will transform hacking 'in months, not years'

key_facts.fact: On Monday, the cyber security agencies of the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand issued a rare joint three-page statement warning that frontier AI is rapidly transforming cyber risk and that leaders must act swiftly.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Frontier AI models are anticipated to exceed current industry expectations, fundamentally transforming both offensive and defensive cyber capabilities,' the intelligence alliance commonly known as the Five Eyes said in a three-page statement on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The statement said the timeline for AI-supercharged offensive cyber capabilities 'is not years, it is months,' urging leaders to prioritize foundational security controls and integrate AI into their defenses.
key_facts.excerpt: Frontier Al models are anticipated to exceed current industry expectations, fundamentally transforming both offensive and defensive cyber capabilities. The timeline is not years, it is months.

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported the warning reflects officials' growing concern over models such as Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber, said to let users execute complex and potentially devastating hacks.
key_facts.excerpt: The warning was another indication of officials' increasing concerns over models such as Anthropic's Mythos or OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber, which are said to allow users to quickly execute complex - and potentially devastating - hacks.

key_facts.fact: The statement follows the US government ordering Anthropic to disable a version of Mythos for foreign nationals, and CISA - a co-signer - cutting deadlines for officials to fix serious vulnerabilities to three days, citing AI threats.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic was forced to disable a version of Mythos after the US government ordered it to suspend access to the models for foreign nationals... the US cyber-defence agency, CISA, which was among those co-signing Monday's statement, reduced the deadlines imposed on government officials to deal with serious digital vulnerabilities in their networks to three days.

stories.headline: Global tech rout: South Korea's Kospi crashes 10%, Nikkei falls 3.5% as AI-chip selloff spreads

key_facts.fact: South Korea's Kospi index closed down 9.99% (910.71 points) at 8,203.84 on Tuesday June 23, its biggest daily plunge since March 4 and the second-largest daily fall of the year; the Korea Exchange triggered a circuit breaker after the index fell more than 8%.
key_facts.excerpt: the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) plunged 910.71 points, or 9.99 percent, to close at 8,203.84... The Korea Exchange (KRX), the bourse operator, activated a circuit breaker at around 2:33 p.m. after the KOSPI plummeted more than 8 percent.

key_facts.fact: Chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell more than 12% (12.31% and 12.47%), triggering an automatic 20-minute bourse-wide trading halt; foreign investors were net sellers of roughly 4 trillion won.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung and SK Hynix shed more than 12 per cent each, triggering an automatic 20-minute bourse-wide trading halt in the afternoon.

key_facts.fact: The rout spread across Asia: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed down 3.55% at 69,788.38 and Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell about 2%; MSCI's gauge of regional equities declined more than 2% after closing at a record high Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: In Japan, the Nikkei 225 was down 3.55 per cent at closing, falling to 69,788.38.

key_facts.fact: In Europe, the pan-European Stoxx 600 shed 1.2% in early trading with its Technology index down 3.2%; STMicroelectronics and ASMI both fell more than 7%, while Nasdaq 100 futures lost 2.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: The Stoxx 600 Technology index led regional losses, with a decline of 3.2%. Chipmaker STMicroelectronics and Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASMI were both down more than 7%... futures tied to New York's Nasdaq 100 index... lost 2.7%.

key_facts.fact: The selloff followed a tech-led drop on Wall Street Monday where the Nasdaq Composite fell about 1.3% as investors rotated out of 'Magnificent Seven' stocks; a local report said SK Hynix is slowing AI memory chip expansion and shifting to cheaper commodity DRAM.
key_facts.excerpt: A local media report said SK Hynix is slowing expansion of AI memory chip production and shifting emphasis to the cheaper commodity DRAM.

stories.headline: Nvidia launches Halos for Robotics, a full-stack safety system bringing AV-grade safety to humanoids

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced Halos for Robotics on June 22, 2026, described as the industry's first full-stack, open robotics safety system that extends Nvidia's autonomous-vehicle safety architecture to humanoids, industrial robots and autonomous mobile robots.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA Halos for Robotics is the industry's only full-stack, open robotics safety system, extending NVIDIA Halos' proven autonomous vehicle safety to robotics and physical AI.

key_facts.fact: The platform pairs Nvidia IGX Thor hardware and Holoscan Sensor Bridge for AI compute with Halos OS (including Halos Core, a safety OS running Linux and QNX), leveraging over a decade of AV safety R&D, 18,000 engineering years and 21 billion safety transistors.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA launched the Halos for Robotics platform, integrating AI compute (IGX Thor) and a comprehensive safety OS (Halos OS), leveraging over a decade of AV safety R&D, including 18,000 engineering years and 21 billion safety transistors.

key_facts.fact: Agility Robotics is the first to use Halos for Robotics, integrating IGX Thor and Halos Core into the safe human-detection system of its humanoid Digit; Digit will be the first production robot shipping with Nvidia Halos OS, operating in warehouse environments alongside people.
key_facts.excerpt: Digit, Agility's humanoid, will be the first production robot shipping with NVIDIA Halos OS. It will operate in real warehouse environments, using NVIDIA IGX and Halos Core to safely navigate and work alongside people.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also opened the Halos AI Systems Inspection Lab, the world's first ANAB-accredited program for functional and AI safety in both autonomous vehicles and robotics, working with certification bodies including TÜV Rheinland, UL Solutions, TÜV SÜD, exida, SGS and CertX.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nvidia Halos AI Systems Inspection Lab is the world's first ANSI National Accreditation Board (ANAB)-accredited program for physical AI functional and AI safety, helping partners prepare Halos integrations for third-party certification by leading certification bodies including TÜV Rheinland, UL Solutions, TÜV SÜD, exida, SGS and CertX.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases full GPT-5.5-Cyber and launches Patch the Planet with Trail of Bits

key_facts.excerpt: Patch the Planet is an initiative built to help maintainers move from findings to fixes. Founded with Trail of Bits, and in collaboration with HackerOne and Calif, we are funding expert security researchers and equipping them with Codex Security and our advanced models.

stories.headline: Oracle says AI adoption helped cut 21,000 jobs in past year, per annual filing

key_facts.excerpt: Oracle reduced its workforce by 13% over the past 12 months and cited AI deployment in an annual filing on Monday. The company currently employs 141,000 full-time workers, down from 162,000 the previous year.

key_facts.fact: Oracle's filing stated that 'the adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce,' Oracle said on Monday (Jun 22) in an annual financial regulatory filing.

key_facts.fact: The cuts led to about $1.8 billion in severance and restructuring costs over the past year, up sharply from a $374 million restructuring bill the prior year.
key_facts.excerpt: The firm said the cuts have led to about $1.8bn (£1.36bn) in severance payments and other restructuring costs in the past year... The sum is significantly higher than the $374m restructuring bill in the previous financial year.

key_facts.fact: The reductions come as Oracle faces financial pressure from an expensive build-out of AI data centers for customers such as OpenAI and Meta; the company joins peers whose collective AI capex plans could reach $700 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle joins several tech giants, including Meta, Google, Microsoft and Amazon, who have announced capex plans that could reach $700 billion to fuel their AI data center developments.

stories.headline: Sakana AI launches Fugu, a multi-agent orchestrator that behaves like a single model

key_facts.fact: Japanese startup Sakana AI publicly released Fugu on Monday, a multi-agent orchestration system delivered as a single foundation model accessible through one OpenAI-compatible API; it ships in two variants, Fugu and Fugu Ultra.
key_facts.excerpt: Japanese startup Sakana AI announced Monday the public release of the Sakana Fugu service that combines multiple artificial intelligence models into one collaborative workflow.

key_facts.fact: Rather than being a standalone model, Fugu dynamically routes queries to a swappable pool of specialized AI agents, deciding whether to answer directly or assemble and coordinate a team of expert models internally.
key_facts.excerpt: Fugu (Japanese for 'pufferfish'), bypasses the traditional monolithic model structure by dynamically routing queries to a swappable pool of specialized AI agents.

key_facts.fact: Sakana says Fugu Ultra exceeds Claude Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench (Fugu Ultra 93.2, Fugu 92.9, Fable 89.8) and beats Mythos Preview on GPQA-Diamond (Fugu Ultra 95.5, Mythos Preview 94.6), claiming parity with frontier models without export-control exposure.
key_facts.excerpt: Fugu actually exceeds the performance of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench (Fugu Ultra: 93.2, Fugu: 92.9, Fable: 89.8), and beats the prior Claude Mythos Preview model on GPQA-D (Fugu Ultra: 95.5, Fugu: 95.5, Mythos Preview: 94.6).

key_facts.fact: Sakana frames Fugu as a hedge against vendor lock-in and export controls, noting access to top models 'can disappear overnight' and that orchestrating a swappable agent pool routes around vendor restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: Relying on a single company's model for national infrastructure is a massive risk. As recent export controls have shown, access to top models can disappear overnight... Fugu simply routes around vendor restrictions by relying on an entirely swappable agent pool.

key_facts.fact: Fugu Ultra went live on Vercel's AI Gateway as 'sakana/fugu-ultra' on Monday, June 22.
key_facts.excerpt: Our Fugu models surpass publicly accessible frontier models and are shoulder-to-shoulder with Fable 5 and Mythos Preview in various rigorous engineering, scientific, and reasoning benchmarks while delivering frontier capability without the risk of export controls.

stories.headline: SpaceX launches debut $20B+ bond sale, discloses $100.8B cash; stock extends post-IPO slide

key_facts.fact: SpaceX on Monday June 22 announced its first-ever senior unsecured notes offering, targeting at least $20 billion with maturities of five to 30 years, to repay its bridge loan and for general corporate purposes.
key_facts.excerpt: At least $20 billion is the target for the offering, with bonds maturing across a range spanning five to 30 years. SpaceX said in its SEC filing that it intends to use the net proceeds to repay outstanding borrowings under its bridge loan facility in full.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX disclosed it held approximately $100.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents as of June 19, 2026, and received investment-grade ratings: Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, and S&P BBB.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX disclosed in its filing that it held approximately $100.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents as of June 19, 2026. The company received investment-grade ratings from all three major ratings agencies... Moody's Ratings assigned a Baa1 rating, Fitch Ratings assigned BBB+, and S&P Global Ratings assigned BBB.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX stock fell about 16% on Monday in its third straight losing session, having lost nearly 24% over three days, after a record IPO that priced at $135 per share, raised nearly $86 billion (after greenshoe), and made Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX stock fell 16% on Monday, continuing a selloff that has seen shares tumble over the past three full days of trading after an initial rally from its record-breaking initial public offering.

key_facts.fact: Proceeds will help fund SpaceX's AI and data-center buildout, including plans to eventually build data centers in space; the bridge loan accounts for the bulk of SpaceX's roughly $29.1 billion in long-term debt.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is looking to fund its sweeping AI plans, which includes eventually building data centers in space.

stories.headline: SpaceX signs $6.3B compute deal giving Reflection AI access to Nvidia GB300s at Colossus 2

key_facts.fact: SpaceX signed a computing deal with open-source startup Reflection AI granting immediate access to Nvidia GB300 chips at the Colossus 2 data center, with Reflection paying $150 million per month from July 1, 2026 through 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Reflection will get immediate access to Nvidia GB300s... and has agreed to pay SpaceX $150 million per month beginning July 1, 2026, through 2029, according to materials viewed by CNBC.

key_facts.fact: The payments total about $6.3 billion if the agreement runs through the end of its term, though either company can end the contract with 90 days' notice after the first three months.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is worth up to $6.3 billion and either company has the option to end the contract with 90 days' notice after the first three months.

key_facts.fact: The Reflection deal is smaller than SpaceX's prior Colossus deals: Anthropic pays about $1.25 billion per month and Google $920 million per month, both also running through July 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is smaller than SpaceX's deals with Anthropic and Google, which cost the companies $1.25 billion per month and $920 million per month, respectively.

key_facts.fact: Reflection AI, last valued at $25 billion, is building American open-source AI models to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google; the Colossus data center was originally built by xAI, now part of SpaceX, which has turned it into a commercial compute platform.

stories.headline: US and Iran conclude first round of Switzerland talks; US suspends sanctions, releases $12B in frozen funds

key_facts.fact: The first round of high-level US-Iran talks in Buergenstock, Switzerland concluded Monday June 22 after 18 hours of negotiations, with mediators Qatar and Pakistan saying the two sides agreed to a roadmap toward a final deal within 60 days.
key_facts.excerpt: The first round of talks between high-ranking U.S. and Iranian officials in Switzerland ended Monday... A joint statement from mediating nations Qatar and Pakistan said the U.S. and Iran agreed to a roadmap toward a final deal within 60 days. Technical talks will continue for the rest of the week.

key_facts.fact: The US suspended sanctions against Iran on Monday and, per Iranian state media on Tuesday, Washington agreed to release $12 billion in frozen Iranian funds and temporarily suspend sanctions on Iranian oil.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of their deal, Washington agreed to release $12 billion in frozen funds to Iran, Iranian state media reported on Tuesday, and temporarily suspend sanctions on oil from the Islamic republic.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran committed to free and open transit in the Strait of Hormuz and to permit IAEA inspectors into the country; the Treasury issued a 60-day license allowing Iran to sell previously sanctioned oil.
key_facts.excerpt: The Treasury Department cited Iran's apparent commitment to allow IAEA inspectors back into the country and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz as justification for issuing a 60-day license allowing Iran to sell previously sanctioned oil.

key_facts.fact: Vice President JD Vance called the day 'good progress' and said Iran agreed to allow international nuclear inspectors back, calling it a 'major milestone'; Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran would agree to 'Major Weapons Inspections.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'In line with the ongoing productive talks in Switzerland, Iran has committed to free and open transit in the Strait of Hormuz and to permit International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors into their country,' Bessent wrote on X.

key_facts.fact: Iran's accounts diverged from the US: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said only 'a very brief discussion took place regarding the nuclear issue,' and Iran said it intends to maintain control over the Strait of Hormuz and continue charging passage fees.
key_facts.excerpt: Tehran voiced Tuesday its intent to maintain control over the vital Strait of Hormuz... Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said for his part that 'a very brief discussion took place regarding the nuclear issue, but there was no discussion of details.'

key_facts.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio was due to start a trip to the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain to discuss the deal and efforts to secure full and free transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was due to start a trip to the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait and Bahrain to discuss the deal and 'efforts to secure full and free safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz,' his spokesman Tommy Pigott said.
